**Jaouad Gharib** ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): جواد غريب, born 22 May 1972 in [Khenifra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khenifra "Khenifra"), [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco")) is a [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco")[long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner") who competes in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"). Winner of the [2003 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Championships in Athletics") and [2005 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") over the distance, he is also notable because he only began running seriously at the age of twenty-two. His 2005 retention made him the second successive world championship marathon champion, after [Abel Antón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Ant%C3%B3n "Abel Antón"). He was the silver medallist in the marathon at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics").

Jaouad Gharib was born in [Khenifra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khenifra "Khenifra"), [Middle Atlas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Atlas "Middle Atlas") to [Berber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berber_people "Berber people") parents but he became an [orphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orphan "Orphan"). His favourite sport as a child was [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") and it was not until 1992, when he watched the [Marrakech Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakech_Marathon "Marrakech Marathon") live on television, that he began to take an interest in [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)"). His talent for [long-distance running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") quickly became apparent as he won races for the [Moroccan Royal Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moroccan_Royal_Guard "Moroccan Royal Guard") as well as other national level competitions.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Focus-1) Gharib made his first international competitions in 2001, taking ninth at the [2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") and eleventh in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") at the [2001 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2001 World Championships in Athletics"). He won the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") on the track at the [2001 Mediterranean Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2001_Mediterranean_Games "Athletics at the 2001 Mediterranean Games").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2) Former athletes [Aziz Daouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aziz_Daouda?action=edit&redlink=1 "Aziz Daouda (page does not exist)") and [Brahim Boutayeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahim_Boutayeb "Brahim Boutayeb") convinced Gharib to focus on longer road events, sensing his potential for further distances.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Focus-1)

He ran at the [2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") the following year and a tenth-place finish in the long race gained him a team [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") with the Moroccan men, which was led by [Abderrahim Goumri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abderrahim_Goumri "Abderrahim Goumri").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-3) He scored a [silver medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") at the [2002 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2002 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") as he set a personal best of 1:00:42 to finish seconds behind the winner [Paul Malakwen Kosgei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Malakwen_Kosgei "Paul Malakwen Kosgei").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-4) An appearance over 10,000 m [2002 African Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2002 African Championships in Athletics") resulted in an eighth-place finish.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2)

### Back-to-back World Champion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaouad_Gharib&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Back-to-back World Champion")]

He made his global indoor debut in the [3000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") at the [2003 IAAF World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2003 IAAF World Indoor Championships"), taking twelfth in the final.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2) Another appearance at the [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2003 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") brought him another team bronze, although he managed only 23rd place on that occasion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-5) His appearance at that competition was made at the behest of the Moroccan team director and he took part merely as preparation for his impending debut over the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") distance. Following the coaching of former Olympic champion Brahim Boutayeb, he took part in the [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") a month later, running a time of 2:09:15 for sixth.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-6) Following a [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") win in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), he entered the marathon race at the [2003 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Championships in Athletics"). Despite it being only his second outing over the distance, he saw off [Michael Kosgei Rotich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Kosgei_Rotich "Michael Kosgei Rotich") and [Julio Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Rey "Julio Rey") to forge a lead in the final stages and win the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") in a [Championship record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Championships_in_Athletics_records "List of World Championships in Athletics records") time of 2:08:31.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-8)

He continued to focus on [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") in 2004, beginning with a run of 59:56 minutes at the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") for fourth place on the downhill course.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-9) Next came the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), where he finished third behind [Evans Rutto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evans_Rutto "Evans Rutto") and [Sammy Korir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Korir "Sammy Korir") and set a personal best of 2:07:02 despite slipping and banging his head mid-race.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-10) He competed at his first Olympics at the [2004 Athens Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics") but failed to match his previous global form and finished in eleventh place in the men's marathon.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-11) A groin injury in the run-up to the competition and Gharib reflected that he had pushed himself too much in training during the two weeks before the race.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Assassin-12)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG/250px-2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG)

Gharib and [Patrick Ivuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ivuti "Patrick Ivuti") in a sprint finish at the 2007 [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon")

He repeated his approach to the season in 2005 by starting at the Lisbon Half Marathon and he finished sixth on this occasion.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-13) He ran sub-2:08 at the London Marathon for a second time and improved one place from the previous year, finishing as runner-up behind [Martin Lel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lel "Martin Lel").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-14) His focus of the year was a defence of his title at the [2005 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics"). He returned home to Morocco and trained at altitude in the [Atlas Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlas_Mountains "Atlas Mountains") region. The move proved fruitful as, in spite of a sleepless night and stomach pains during the competition, he won the world championship marathon with an eleven-second margin over runner-up [Christopher Isengwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Isengwe "Christopher Isengwe").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Assassin-12) This made him only the second runner ever to retain the world marathon title, after Spaniard [Abel Antón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Ant%C3%B3n "Abel Antón").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-15)

With no major competition to work towards in 2006, he focused on competing on the circuit. He finished the London Marathon in a time of 2:08:45 – the third fastest run of his career at that point – but this was only enough for eighth in a fast race which saw him beaten by compatriot [Hicham Chatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hicham_Chatt "Hicham Chatt").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-16) After a fourth-place finish at the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run"), his next marathon race came at the [Fukuoka Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukuoka_Marathon "Fukuoka Marathon") in Japan. Gharib came close to a career best, crossing the line in 2:07:19, and took third place on the podium behind [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie") and [Dmytro Baranovskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmytro_Baranovskyy "Dmytro Baranovskyy").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-17)

He had his third sub-2:08 clocking at the London Marathon in 2007, recording 2:07:54 for fourth place. At the [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") later that year he came close to victory but a [photo finish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photo_finish "Photo finish") between Gharib and [Patrick Ivuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ivuti "Patrick Ivuti") resulted in the Moroccan being declared the runner-up.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-18) Gharib won the [silver medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") in the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") marathon held in Beijing, China, giving him his first Olympic medal. Gharib improved his personal best to 2:05:27 at the 2009 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), finishing in third place.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-19) He also finished in third place at the 2009 [NYC Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Marathon "NYC Marathon").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-20)

Running in the [2010 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_London_Marathon "2010 London Marathon"), he had to endure stomach problems but still made the podium, coming home in another third-place finish with a time of 2:06:55.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-21) He took third place at the Great North Run half marathon in September.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-22) He was victorious at the Fukuoka Marathon in December, completing a solo run on the hot course to win in a time of 2:08:24.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-23) The [2011 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_London_Marathon "2011 London Marathon") was a particularly fast race and his time of 2:08:26 left him in sixth and almost four minutes behind winner [Emmanuel Mutai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mutai "Emmanuel Mutai").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-24)

**Jaouad Gharib** ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): جواد غريب, born 22 May 1972 in [Khenifra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khenifra "Khenifra"), [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco")) is a [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco")[long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner") who competes in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"). Winner of the [2003 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Championships in Athletics") and [2005 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") over the distance, he is also notable because he only began running seriously at the age of twenty-two. His 2005 retention made him the second successive world championship marathon champion, after [Abel Antón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Ant%C3%B3n "Abel Antón"). He was the silver medallist in the marathon at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics").

Jaouad Gharib was born in [Khenifra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khenifra "Khenifra"), [Middle Atlas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Atlas "Middle Atlas") to [Berber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berber_people "Berber people") parents but he became an [orphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orphan "Orphan"). His favourite sport as a child was [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") and it was not until 1992, when he watched the [Marrakech Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakech_Marathon "Marrakech Marathon") live on television, that he began to take an interest in [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)"). His talent for [long-distance running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") quickly became apparent as he won races for the [Moroccan Royal Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moroccan_Royal_Guard "Moroccan Royal Guard") as well as other national level competitions.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Focus-1) Gharib made his first international competitions in 2001, taking ninth at the [2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2001 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") and eleventh in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") at the [2001 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2001 World Championships in Athletics"). He won the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") on the track at the [2001 Mediterranean Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2001_Mediterranean_Games "Athletics at the 2001 Mediterranean Games").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2) Former athletes [Aziz Daouda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aziz_Daouda?action=edit&redlink=1 "Aziz Daouda (page does not exist)") and [Brahim Boutayeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahim_Boutayeb "Brahim Boutayeb") convinced Gharib to focus on longer road events, sensing his potential for further distances.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Focus-1)

He ran at the [2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") the following year and a tenth-place finish in the long race gained him a team [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") with the Moroccan men, which was led by [Abderrahim Goumri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abderrahim_Goumri "Abderrahim Goumri").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-3) He scored a [silver medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") at the [2002 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2002 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") as he set a personal best of 1:00:42 to finish seconds behind the winner [Paul Malakwen Kosgei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Malakwen_Kosgei "Paul Malakwen Kosgei").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-4) An appearance over 10,000 m [2002 African Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2002 African Championships in Athletics") resulted in an eighth-place finish.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2)

### Back-to-back World Champion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaouad_Gharib&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Back-to-back World Champion")]

He made his global indoor debut in the [3000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") at the [2003 IAAF World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2003 IAAF World Indoor Championships"), taking twelfth in the final.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-IAAFBio-2) Another appearance at the [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2003 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") brought him another team bronze, although he managed only 23rd place on that occasion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-5) His appearance at that competition was made at the behest of the Moroccan team director and he took part merely as preparation for his impending debut over the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") distance. Following the coaching of former Olympic champion Brahim Boutayeb, he took part in the [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") a month later, running a time of 2:09:15 for sixth.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-6) Following a [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") win in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), he entered the marathon race at the [2003 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2003 World Championships in Athletics"). Despite it being only his second outing over the distance, he saw off [Michael Kosgei Rotich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Kosgei_Rotich "Michael Kosgei Rotich") and [Julio Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Rey "Julio Rey") to forge a lead in the final stages and win the [gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") in a [Championship record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Championships_in_Athletics_records "List of World Championships in Athletics records") time of 2:08:31.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-8)

He continued to focus on [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") in 2004, beginning with a run of 59:56 minutes at the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") for fourth place on the downhill course.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-9) Next came the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), where he finished third behind [Evans Rutto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evans_Rutto "Evans Rutto") and [Sammy Korir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Korir "Sammy Korir") and set a personal best of 2:07:02 despite slipping and banging his head mid-race.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-10) He competed at his first Olympics at the [2004 Athens Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics") but failed to match his previous global form and finished in eleventh place in the men's marathon.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-11) A groin injury in the run-up to the competition and Gharib reflected that he had pushed himself too much in training during the two weeks before the race.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Assassin-12)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG/250px-2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2007_Chicago_Marathon_final_200M_-_men-2.JPG)

Gharib and [Patrick Ivuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ivuti "Patrick Ivuti") in a sprint finish at the 2007 [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon")

He repeated his approach to the season in 2005 by starting at the Lisbon Half Marathon and he finished sixth on this occasion.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-13) He ran sub-2:08 at the London Marathon for a second time and improved one place from the previous year, finishing as runner-up behind [Martin Lel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lel "Martin Lel").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-14) His focus of the year was a defence of his title at the [2005 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics"). He returned home to Morocco and trained at altitude in the [Atlas Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlas_Mountains "Atlas Mountains") region. The move proved fruitful as, in spite of a sleepless night and stomach pains during the competition, he won the world championship marathon with an eleven-second margin over runner-up [Christopher Isengwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Isengwe "Christopher Isengwe").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-Assassin-12) This made him only the second runner ever to retain the world marathon title, after Spaniard [Abel Antón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Ant%C3%B3n "Abel Antón").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-15)

With no major competition to work towards in 2006, he focused on competing on the circuit. He finished the London Marathon in a time of 2:08:45 – the third fastest run of his career at that point – but this was only enough for eighth in a fast race which saw him beaten by compatriot [Hicham Chatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hicham_Chatt "Hicham Chatt").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-16) After a fourth-place finish at the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run"), his next marathon race came at the [Fukuoka Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukuoka_Marathon "Fukuoka Marathon") in Japan. Gharib came close to a career best, crossing the line in 2:07:19, and took third place on the podium behind [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie") and [Dmytro Baranovskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmytro_Baranovskyy "Dmytro Baranovskyy").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-17)

He had his third sub-2:08 clocking at the London Marathon in 2007, recording 2:07:54 for fourth place. At the [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") later that year he came close to victory but a [photo finish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photo_finish "Photo finish") between Gharib and [Patrick Ivuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ivuti "Patrick Ivuti") resulted in the Moroccan being declared the runner-up.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-18) Gharib won the [silver medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") in the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") marathon held in Beijing, China, giving him his first Olympic medal. Gharib improved his personal best to 2:05:27 at the 2009 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), finishing in third place.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-19) He also finished in third place at the 2009 [NYC Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NYC_Marathon "NYC Marathon").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-20)

Running in the [2010 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_London_Marathon "2010 London Marathon"), he had to endure stomach problems but still made the podium, coming home in another third-place finish with a time of 2:06:55.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-21) He took third place at the Great North Run half marathon in September.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-22) He was victorious at the Fukuoka Marathon in December, completing a solo run on the hot course to win in a time of 2:08:24.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaouad_Gharib#cite_note-23) The [2011 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_London_Marathon "2011 London Marathon") was a particularly fast race and his time of 2:08:26 left him in sixth and almost four minutes behind winner [Emmanuel Mutai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mutai "Emmanuel Mutai").[[24]](

French long-distance runner

**Mohamed Ouaadi** (born 1 January 1969 in [Tiznit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiznit "Tiznit"), Morocco) is a retired French long-distance runner who specialized in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

French long-distance runner

**Mohamed Ouaadi** (born 1 January 1969 in [Tiznit](link_2), Morocco) is a retired French long-distance runner who specialized in the [marathon](link_3).

**Addis Abebe** ([Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): አዲስ አበበ; born September 5, 1970) is a former [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner") from [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia"), best known for winning a [bronze medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") event at the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics").

In the 1988 World Junior Championships, Abebe won the gold medal in the 10,000 metres and a bronze in the 5,000 meters events.

**Addis Abebe** ([Amharic](link_13): አዲስ አበበ; born September 5, 1970) is a former [long-distance runner](link_14) from [Ethiopia](link_5), best known for winning a [bronze medal](link_15) in the [10,000 metres](link_16) event at the [1992 Summer Olympics](link_8).

In the 1988 World Junior Championships, Abebe won the gold medal in the 10,000 metres and a bronze in the 5,000 meters events.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

South African long-distance runner

**Abner Chipu** (born 2 January 1972) is a retired [South African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") long-distance runner. His specialties include Cross, Half Marathon, Marathon, Cross team event and the Half Marathon Team Event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abner_Chipu#cite_note-1)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

South African long-distance runner

**Abner Chipu** (born 2 January 1972) is a retired [South African](link_2) long-distance runner. His specialties include Cross, Half Marathon, Marathon, Cross team event and the Half Marathon Team Event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abner_Chipu#cite_note-1)

**Martín Fiz Martín** (born 3 March 1963) is a Spanish former [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Martín Fiz Martín was born on 3 March 1963 in [Vitoria-Gasteiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitoria-Gasteiz "Vitoria-Gasteiz").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Fiz won the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") at the [1994 European Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_European_Athletics_Championships "1994 European Athletics Championships") in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") and repeated his success at the [1995 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Athletics_Championships "1995 World Athletics Championships") in [Gothenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothenburg "Gothenburg"). The same year he captured the title in the [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Rotterdam_Marathon "1995 Rotterdam Marathon").

At the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") in Atlanta Fiz came fourth in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1996_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"). A year later he won a [silver medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") at the [1997 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1997 World Championships in Athletics") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), finishing behind his countryman [Abel Anton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Anton "Abel Anton").

He competed in three consecutive [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics") for his native country, starting in 1992. At the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney Fiz came sixth in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon").

## Post-career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Post-career")]

Fiz has continued running into [masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_athletics "Masters athletics") age divisions, setting the [world M55 record in the road 10K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_masters_world_records_in_road_running#10K_run "List of masters world records in road running") at 31:36 on 13 January 2019 in [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia "Valencia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz#cite_note-1)

He is the only athlete in the world who has managed to win in six Majors Marathons in the Master 50 category (runners over 50 years old), winning the Marathons of New York, Tokyo, Boston, Berlin, Chicago, and London, achieving the goal of obtaining the 'Six World Marathon Majors', [World Marathon Majors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Marathon_Majors "World Marathon Majors"), an international competition created in 2006, which brings together six of the most prestigious world Marathons, recognised as the most high profile on the calendar.

**Martín Fiz Martín** (born 3 March 1963) is a Spanish former [long-distance runner](link_13).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Martín Fiz Martín was born on 3 March 1963 in [Vitoria-Gasteiz](link_14).

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Fiz won the [marathon](link_15) at the [1994 European Athletics Championships](link_11) in [Helsinki](link_16) and repeated his success at the [1995 World Athletics Championships](link_17) in [Gothenburg](link_18). The same year he captured the title in the [Rotterdam Marathon](link_19).

At the [1996 Summer Olympics](link_20) in Atlanta Fiz came fourth in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1996_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_21]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon"). A year later he won a [silver medal](link_22) at the [1997 World Championships in Athletics](link_8) in [Athens](link_23), finishing behind his countryman [Abel Anton](link_24).

He competed in three consecutive [Summer Olympics](link_25) for his native country, starting in 1992. At the [2000 Summer Olympics](link_26) in Sydney Fiz came sixth in the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men [link_27]'s_marathon "Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon").

## Post-career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Post-career")]

Fiz has continued running into [masters](link_28) age divisions, setting the [world M55 record in the road 10K](link_29) at 31:36 on 13 January 2019 in [Valencia](link_30).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Fiz#cite_note-1)

He is the only athlete in the world who has managed to win in six Majors Marathons in the Master 50 category (runners over 50 years old), winning the Marathons of New York, Tokyo, Boston, Berlin, Chicago, and London, achieving the goal of obtaining the 'Six World Marathon Majors', [World Marathon Majors](link_31), an international competition created in 2006, which brings together six of the most prestigious world Marathons, recognised as the most high profile on the calendar.
